gate_VS_drawdown_reconciliation.ruin_note: Under this fixed-notional, non-compounding, absorbing-floor reading, the account is wiped out at bar 49 of 4488 (2010-08-25) and never recovers -- a real difference in kind from the compounding reading, which survives this same stretch because each day's P&L is realized against the CURRENT (already-compounded) equity, not a fixed original base. This is the concrete illustration of why the two conventions diverge this much: a daily-rebalanced, always-reinvested strategy's true real-world equity path is closer to the compounding reading (that IS how a real account marks itself to market daily); the fixed-notional convention designed for this notebook's own episodic single-trade spread bookkeeping produces a materially different, more pessimistic answer when applied to a daily-rebalanced portfolio instead.
gate_VS_drawdown_reconciliation.note: Sharpe and DSR are unchanged (verified above) -- this recomputation touches only the drawdown convention. The published -5.41 log-unit drawdown corresponds to -0.9955 (-99.6%) of peak under a continuously-compounded reading; the fixed-notional, capital-bounded reading (no compounding, floored at zero) gives -1.0000 (-100.0%) of peak instead. This is a labelled hypothetical recomputation, not a replacement of 10b's own published number.
